note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Every count, address, court kind, lighting answer and hours line below comes from one City of Albuquerque page: its pickleball page, whose "Pickleball Court Locations" table gives each venue a name, an address and a description cell that says what kind of court is being counted - "Pickleball Complex" or "Tennis Courts with Pickleball Lines" - and marks lighting where it applies, with a few sentences of prose beneath it on hours, reservations, the ninety-minute rule and lessons. Where the City stays silent - on price, surface, parking, indoor or outdoor, and lighting at twelve of the thirteen venues - this page says so instead of guessing.

slots.parking: The City of Albuquerque publishes nothing about parking at any of the thirteen venues on this page. The word does not appear on the pickleball page, whose table carries a name, an address and a description cell and nothing about the ground around the courts, and the prose beneath the table is about hours, reservations and lessons rather than arrival. Restrooms are not mentioned either, at any venue. This page does not supply either from a map. What the City does publish that shapes a trip is the address, and the addresses are worth a note, because the City writes almost all of them without a street type - "501 Elizabeth SE", "4800 Cherokee NE", "7511 Burke NE" - and the US Census address file supplied one for each: Elizabeth Street, Cherokee Road, Burke Street. All thirteen matched at house-number level as the City writes them, with the compass quadrant the City attaches to every address - NE, NW or SE - carried through unchanged, and none needed a second resolver. The other planning fact is the clock. Two venues have stated hours, 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, and both are the City's dedicated complexes; the other eleven venues have no stated hours at all, and one venue in the whole city has a lighting answer. So at Manzano Mesa and Villela the City tells you when the gate is open, and at every other venue it does not.
slots.peak_hours: The City states hours for two published venues and a rule for all of them. The hours are for the complexes: "Manzano Mesa, Villella, and Pat Hurley are open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily", and of those three Pat Hurley is not published here, so the sentence covers Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex and Villela Pickleball Courts. Sixteen hours a day, stated by the operator, is a wide window. At Manzano Mesa twenty-one of the thirty-three courts are lit, so the late end of it is usable; at Villela the City states no lighting, so whether 10 p.m. means anything in practice is not something the record can say. The rule is on the same page, under "Availability & Reservations": "Courts are typically available on a first come, first serve basis and play is limited to 1.5 hours when others are waiting." That is the closest thing Albuquerque publishes to a peak-hours policy: not when the courts are busy, but what happens when they are. Two things sit outside that rule. Sierra Vista Tennis Complex is the one venue whose courts the City says can be booked, "in advanced by calling 505-767-5445". And whole complexes can be reserved for special events and tournaments through the City's Sports Office, with a Facility Use Agreement and liability insurance required of groups running non-City tournaments, so a tournament day at Manzano Mesa is a day the courts may not be available at all. The City's lessons run there too, on summer weekday mornings at 8, 9 and 10 a.m. in four two-week blocks from 8 June to 31 July, and on spring and autumn Saturdays. What the City does not publish anywhere is when any venue is busy - no league night, no morning rush, no open-play time.
slots.surface_condition: The City names no surface for any pickleball court in Albuquerque. No cell of the table says asphalt, concrete or acrylic, the prose says nothing about what is underfoot, and nothing says indoor or outdoor about any venue, so this page records neither. What the City does state, in the description cell of every row but one, is what kind of court is being counted, and for a player that is the more useful fact. Two venues are a "Pickleball Complex" - Manzano Mesa with thirty-three courts and Villela with six - and the prose calls them the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes". Nine venues are "Tennis Courts with Pickleball Lines", the City's own phrase for a tennis court carrying a second set of lines, and the count in those cells is of pickleball courts marked out, not of tennis courts. Sierra Vista Tennis Complex is "Tennis/Pickleball Courts" with "2 Courts and 4 Lined Courts", which the prose spells out as "2 permanent pickleball courts, and 4 lined pickleball courts". Wells Park's cell says "3 Pickleball Courts" and nothing about their kind, so that one is recorded as unstated rather than assumed either way. Nets are the other thing a lined court raises, and the City's visible page says nothing about them; a sentence about players bringing their own exists only in the page source, inside a comment a browser does not render, and an unpublished sentence is not a published fact. So: forty-one courts the City calls dedicated or permanent, forty-two that are lines on tennis courts, and three it does not characterise, with nothing said about the condition of any of them.
slots.local_scene: Eighty-six verified courts across thirteen City venues, thirty-nine of them at the two dedicated complexes and the rest across eleven parks, most of them tennis courts with pickleball lines. Albuquerque is the first New Mexico city on this site and the first in Bernalillo County. Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex's thirty-three courts is the largest single-venue count on this site; Mesa's Tennis & Pickleball Center, with twenty-one, held that place before this run, and San Antonio's Fairchild Park has eighteen. Eighty-six is one of the largest court totals on the site, second to Seattle's ninety-two. The City's own page says something about who plays here. It names a City Pickleball Manager, 505-224-6693, runs junior and adult lessons at Manzano Mesa with classes "limited to six participants", and describes the ABQ Pickleball Club as a body that "provides tournaments, training, playing opportunities, and conducts pickleball open houses". None of that is a schedule of open play, and the City publishes no open-play time for any venue. What the City does not state matters as much. No price appears for any court - "first come, first serve" is a play format, not a fee, and the Sierra Vista phone reservation carries no stated cost - so no venue here has a fee answer. Lighting is stated at one venue, Manzano Mesa, and nowhere else. Three venues the City lists are not published, and they are named here rather than dropped: Pat Hurley Park, "4 Courts and 4 Lined Courts"; Alamosa Park, "8 Lighted Pickleball Courts"; and Ventana Ranch Park, "12 Lighted Pickleball Courts". Neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap finds the address the City writes for any of the three. That costs twenty-eight courts, twenty of them lit - two of the City's three lighting statements are at venues that cannot be placed. The page source also carries an older version of the table inside a comment a browser does not show, with different counts at four venues and three park names the visible table lacks; nothing from it is treated as a published fact.

best_for.heading: Best if you want the most courts, with lights and stated hours
best_for.text: Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex has thirty-three dedicated courts, twenty-one of them lit, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily in the City's own sentence, at 501 Elizabeth SE. It is the City's lesson venue and the one Albuquerque address where a rotation, an evening game and a stated closing time all rest on published facts. Price, surface and parking are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want dedicated courts at a smaller complex
best_for.text: Villela Pickleball Courts is the second of the City's "two dedicated pickleball complexes": six courts that are pickleball courts whenever you arrive, open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, at 4800 Cherokee NE. Six is enough for a rotation. The City states no lighting here, so the late end of those hours is unverified; price and surface are not stated.

best_for.heading: Best if you want to book a court in advance
best_for.text: Sierra Vista Tennis Complex is the one Albuquerque venue whose courts the City says can be reserved, "in advanced by calling 505-767-5445". Two permanent pickleball courts and four lined onto tennis courts, six in all, at 5001 Montano Rd. NW. No price is stated for a reservation, no hours are stated for the complex, and lighting is not stated.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Albuquerque have?
faqs.a: We have verified 86 across thirteen City venues: 33 at Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, 8 at Lauren C. Bolles, 6 each at Villela, Sierra Vista and Montgomery, 4 each at Columbus, Eagle Ranch, Loma Del Norte, Lynnewood and Quintessence, 3 at Wells Park and 2 each at Hoffman and Rinconada. The City also lists Pat Hurley, Alamosa and Ventana Ranch, 28 courts we cannot publish.

Manzano Mesa Pickleball Complex, where the City's cell reads "33 Courts (21 Lighted)" - twenty-one lit, twelve with no statement. No other published venue carries a lighting answer either way. The City's other two lighting statements, eight lit courts at Alamosa Park and twelve at Ventana Ranch Park, belong to venues whose addresses cannot be resolved, so they do not publish.

faqs.q: Is it free to play in Albuquerque?
faqs.a: Not stated, at any venue. The City publishes no price for any pickleball court; "first come, first serve" describes how a court is taken, not what it costs, and the phone reservation at Sierra Vista carries no stated fee. A court is recorded as free here only when an operator writes that down, and Albuquerque has not.

faqs.q: Why are Pat Hurley Park, Alamosa Park and Ventana Ranch Park not listed?
faqs.a: Because neither the US Census address file nor OpenStreetMap finds the address the City writes for any of them: "3828 Rincon Rd NW", "1100 Bataan SW" and "10000 Universe NW". Between them they hold 28 courts, 20 of them lit, and Pat Hurley has stated hours of 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Each fails on its address alone.

faqs.q: What are the hours, and can I book a court?
faqs.a: The City states hours for two published venues: Manzano Mesa and Villela, "open from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily". The other eleven have none stated. Play is first come, first served with a ninety-minute limit when others are waiting. Only Sierra Vista's courts can be reserved, by phone on 505-767-5445; whole complexes are booked for tournaments through the City's Sports Office.
